contexts.text: The altar and burnt-offering... were the principal things of all representative worship. AC 921. AC 921:end. AC 10143:2.
(Origin of burnt-offerings.)
(Noah) offered burnt-offerings upon the altar () = all worship thence derived... Burnt-offerings, in one complex, = representative worship. Illustrated.
Burnt-offerings = worship from love; sacrifices, worship from the faith thence derived. AC 7857:2. AC 8680.
That Noah offered burnt-offerings is not true but made-up history, because burnt-offerings = what is holy of worship.
Under Bread, see this reference.

The burnt-offerings and sacrifices in the Jewish Church represented nothing but the celestial things which are of the Lord's Kingdom... in general, all those things which are of love and charity, for these are celestial things; and each kind of sacrifice represented something in particular... AC 2177.
The primary thing of representative worship consisted of burnt-offerings and sacrifices.

Offer (Isaac) for a burnt-offering () = that He should sanctify Himself with the Divine. The burnt-offering with the Hebrew nation, and in the Jewish Church, was the most holy thing of their worship... and their sanctifications were effected thereby...
It is the general belief at this day that the burnt-offerings and sacrifices signified the Lord's passion...
Where is the cattle for a burnt-offering? () = where are those of the human race who are to be sanctified?
He offered it for a burnt-offering instead of his son = the sanctification and adoption of them. To offer for a burnt-offering = to be sanctified.
Under Lamb, see these references. AC 7839:end. AC 9295:2. AC 10133.

Jethro... took a burnt-offering and sacrifices for God () = worship from the good of love and truths of faith... The reason burnt-offerings represented those things which are of the good of love, and sacrifices those things which are of the truth of faith, is evident from the regulation of them; namely, that in the burnt-offerings all things were consumed, both the flesh and the blood, but in the sacrifices the flesh was eaten. Illustrated... The reason these two things were represented by the burnt-offerings and sacrifices, was that the burnt-offerings and sacrifices represented all the worship of God in general, and the worship of God in general is founded upon love and faith... AC 9714.

Thou shalt sacrifice upon (the altar of earth) thy burnt-offering and thy peace-offerings () = worship in special according to the spiritual life of each one. Burnt-offerings and sacrifices = all internal worship in general, with variety according to the various kinds of celestial and spiritual things... Hence it was that such various kinds of sacrifices were instituted. Enumerated.

They offered burnt-offerings and sacrificed peace sacrifices of bullocks to Jehovah () = a representative of the worship of the Lord from good, and from the truth which is from good. Burnt-offerings and sacrifices = the worship of the Lord in general; specifically, burnt-offerings = the worship of the Lord from the good of love; and sacrifices, from the truth of faith which is from good.
Under Meat-offering, see this reference.

The purifications of the external man were represented by burnt-offerings and sacrifices of oxen, bullocks, and he-goats; and the purifications of the internal man by burnt-offerings and sacrifices of rams, kids, and she-goats; but the purification of the very internal itself which is inmost, by those of lambs. AC 10042:13.

The implantation of good and truth in the external or natural man is signified by the sacrifice of a bullock; and the implantation and conjunction of good and truth in the internal or spiritual man by the burnt-offering of a ram (). AC 10048.
Under Sacrifice, see this reference.

It is a burnt-offering to Jehovah () = the glorification of the Lord's Human. Burnt-offering = the glorification of the Lord's Human... The sacrifices signified purification from evils and falsities, and the implantation of truth; but the burnt-offering, the conjunction of truth with good, thus plenary regeneration; and in the supreme sense, in which the Lord is treated of, the sacrifices signified the casting out of evils and falsities from His human which He had from the mother, and the implantation of Divine truth from the Divine good which is in Him; and the burnt-offerings, the unition of Divine truth with Divine good, which unition is what is meant by glorification...
The reason the burnt-offering is called an odour of rest to Jehovah () is that by the burnt-offering was represented the unition of the Lord's Divine Human with the Divine itself...
Under Flesh, see this reference.
Thou shalt... burn them on the altar upon the burnt-offering () = unition with the Divine good of the Divine love... By the burnt-offering is signified and described the conjunction itself.
The daily burnt-offerings represented in general that which concerns the reception of the Lord. Explained.
A continual burnt-offering () = all Divine worship in general. Burnt-offering = Divine worship.

Nor burnt-offering and meat-offering () = no representative of regeneration there by means of the truths and goods of celestial love. Burnt-offering = a representative of purification from evils, of the implantation of good and truth, and of their conjunction; thus of regeneration. References.

They offered burnt-offerings and brought peace-offerings () = the worship of their own loves, thus of their delights, and of the falsities thence derived... In the opposite sense, burnt-offerings = worship from man's Own loves, which worship is from the delights of those loves, which are evils; and sacrifices = worship from the falsities thence derived...
The kine together with the cart being offered for a burnt-offering, signified that thus the Lord was propitiated.
Burnt-offerings in general signified the worship of the Lord from the good of love (the sacrifices, from truths thence derived). AE 391:16. AE 444:7.
Burnt-offering = worship from celestial good; sacrifice, worship from spiritual good. AE 491:3.

As the burnt-offerings and sacrifices signified celestial and spiritual things respectively, the burnt-offerings were made of whole males, of either the flock or the herd; but the sacrifices, of either males or females. Illustrated, Explained.
